pages.text: The forced systems let a pack maker declare that a specific item or mob is $(l)always$() elemental, without touching the enchanting table.$(br2)On items, a forced element is realised as a real enchantment: it is applied automatically once the item is in a player's inventory, and tracked in the item's custom data so it can be updated or stripped later.

pages.title: forced_weapons
pages.text: In $(thing)elementalcraft-forced-items.toml$():$(br2)$(thing)"modid:item_id,element"$()$(br2)Example:$(br2)$(thing)"minecraft:golden_sword,thunder"$()$(br2)The item gains that Aspect at level I whenever a player carries it. Removing the line strips the enchantment again on the next inventory check.

pages.title: forced_armor
pages.text: In the same file:$(br2)$(thing)"modid:item_id,enh_element,enh_points,res_element,res_points"$()$(br2)Example:$(br2)$(thing)"minecraft:iron_chestplate,frost,50,fire,25"$()$(br2)Points may be a single number or a range such as $(thing)20-60$(); ranges are rolled from the tier weights in the common config. Player items are capped at $(thing)level V per piece$().

pages.title: forced_entities
pages.text: In $(thing)elementalcraft-common.toml$() -> $(thing)forced_attributes.forced_entities$():$(br2)$(thing)"modid:entity_id,attack,enh_element,enh_points,res_element,res_points"$()$(br2)Example:$(br2)$(thing)"minecraft:zombie,fire,fire,60,frost,40"$()$(br2)This replaces random generation for that mob. Note that the $(thing)Nether$() and $(thing)End$() dimension overrides are applied to any mob that has no forced entry, so add entries there if you want exceptions.
